 ----Petitioner  Versus State of Rajasthan, through Public Prosecutor  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Sukha Dev  Mr. Kshitij Vyas For Respondent(s) : Mr. Hathi Singh Jodha, Public  Prosecutor  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA PRAKASH SHRIMALI Order 09/05/2025

This application for bail under Section 483 of BNSS (439 Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.209/2023, registered at Police Station Ambapura, District - Banswara for the offences under Sections 363, 366, 344, 376(2)(N) of the IPC and Sections 5(j)(ii)/6 and 5(l)/6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act,
2012 and Section 84 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the allegation against the accused-petitioner is of committing rape with the prosecutrix due to which she got pregnant.
The [2025:RJ-JD:22426] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-4834/2025] prosecutrix has given birth to a female child which is about 2 months old.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the matter has been compromised between both the parties and the petitioner has married with the prosecutrix.
He filed an affidavit dated 03.04.2025 of the prosecutrix in this regard.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 25.09.2024 and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-petitioner.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that accused-petitioner has committed a heinous crime of rape with the prosecutrix due to which she got pregnant.
She has also gave birth to a female child which is about two months old.
The prosecutrix is minor.

Therefore, looking to the gravity of the offence, the accused- petitioner may Kailash vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:22426) on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55893941/
1 not be enlarged on bail.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case; the compromise arrived at between the parties; and considering the affidavit of the prosecutrix; without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 483 of BNSS (439 Cr.P.C.) is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Kailash S/o Madia, arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.209/2023,
registered at Police Station Ambapura, District - Banswara, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and [2025:RJ-JD:22426] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-4834/2025] two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
Affidavit dated 03.04.2025 and the compromise-deed are taken on record.
(CHANDRA PRAKASH SHRIMALI),J 128-Ravi Khandelwal Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
